statement.p: A horizontal square has sides of 1600 km running north-south and east-west. A wind blows from the west and increases in magnitude toward the north at a rate of 2 m/s for every 800 km. Compute the circulation of the wind counterclockwise around the square.

static.solution:
v meter/sec on the south side and (v + 4) meter/sec on the north side.
The circulation is the sum of the line integrals along the four sides of the square. The line integrals along the eastern and western edges are both zero, since the wind velocity is perpendicular to these edges. The integral to the right along the south side equals (1600\mbox{ km})(- v \mbox{ m/s})= - 1.6 v \times 10^{6} \mbox{ m}^2/\mbox{s}, and the integral to the left along the north side equals (-1600\mbox{ km})(-(v + 4) \mbox{ m/s}) = 1.6(v + 4) \times 10^{6} \mbox{ m}^2/\mbox{s}. The total circulation is then the sum of these, \mbox{circulation} = -1.6 v \times 10^{6} + 1.6(v + 4) \times 10^{6} = -6.4 \times 10^{6} \mbox{ m}^2/\mbox{s}.
